value.notes: null (or any non-finite value) makes the component indeterminate — there is no isIndeterminate prop.

Value.children.type: ((formattedValue: string | null, value: number | null) => React.ReactNode) | null

dataAttributes: data-complete — value has reached max (Root, Label, Track, Indicator, Value)
data-progressing — value is between min and max

controlledProps: value (required, so Progress is always fully controlled)
controlled.note: No defaultValue and no change callback at all — Progress is a display component; you own the value state.

formIntegration.note: Not a form control: no name, no submission, no validation.

keyboard.keys: None — role="progressbar" is a non-interactive role.

notableDifferences: React Aria's ProgressBar takes isIndeterminate; Base UI derives indeterminacy from value={null} and REQUIRES the value prop.
The label/value/track/indicator are separate parts that you place and lay out yourself; React Aria renders them from props with slots.
React Aria exposes formatOptions + a label; Base UI has format/locale, Progress.Label and a render-prop Progress.Value.
React Aria's data-indeterminate/data-complete equivalents exist, but Base UI adds data-progressing as the third state, driven by a status: 'indeterminate' | 'progressing' | 'complete' state string.
